title: Asynchronous FIFO
constraints: 8 entries × 8 bits, with independent, unrelated write and read clocks. Each side has its own synchronous reset (asserted together at start-up).
A write happens on a rising `wclk` edge with `winc && !wfull`. A read (pop) happens on a rising `rclk` edge with `rinc && !rempty`. Requests while full or empty are ignored.
`rdata` always shows the **oldest** entry while `rempty = 0` (first-word fall-through, combinational read of the memory).

Pointers cross domains through **2-flop synchronizers**: an entry may not become readable earlier than 2 `rclk` edges after it was written, and a freed slot may not be reused earlier than 2 `wclk` edges after the read. Flags are therefore pessimistic, but never wrong: no overflow, no underflow. With the reader idle, the FIFO must accept exactly 8 writes. Tested with a fast writer / slow reader and the reverse.
hints: Keep 4-bit binary pointers (3 address bits + 1 wrap bit). Convert them to Gray code and pass the Gray pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer into the other domain.
Empty: the next read Gray pointer equals the synchronized write Gray pointer. Full: the next write Gray pointer equals the synchronized read Gray pointer with its **two MSBs inverted**.
Register the flags from the *next* pointer values so that they update in the same cycle as the pointers.
Why Gray? A pointer sampled mid-change is off by at most one, which is either the old or the new value, both safe.
